owner_posts.post_text: From 2028, USMLE Step 1, Step 2 CK, and Step 3 will be available on 45 fixed testing dates each year instead of the current on-demand schedule. This update is being introduced to improve exam security. There are no changes to exam eligibility or syllabus. Indian IMGs should plan their exam dates early, especially for Step 2 CK, and book their preferred slots as soon as registration opens because seats may fill quickly. Be sure to check the official 2028 testing calendar.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has announced that PG Diploma admissions will end after the 2026–27 academic session, with all diploma seats being upgraded to MD/MS programs. Students currently enrolled in diploma courses will not be affected. Medical colleges wishing to convert diploma seats must seek approval from MARB. As the 2026–27 batch will be the final cycle for PG Diploma admissions, NEET PG aspirants should plan ahead for a degree-only postgraduate admission process from 2027–28, where competition is expected to increase.

Beginning in June 2026, the USMLE has expanded nutrition-related content across Steps 1, 2, and 3, in line with recommendations published in JAMA in 2024. Indian IMGs can expect more questions on clinical nutrition, particularly micronutrient deficiencies, drug-nutrient interactions, and nutrition issues across different stages of life. Nutrition-specific performance feedback will now be included in score reports for Steps 2 and 3, while Step 1 remains pass/fail without detailed nutrition reporting. There is no need to worry-simply incorporate nutrition concepts into your preparation using resources such as UWorld, First Aid, and strong clinical reasoning skills.

Failed FMGE? You're not alone-only about 25% of candidates cleared the January 2026 session. The good news is that your medical career can still move forward. International licensing pathways such as USMLE (USA), PLAB/UKMLA (UK), and AMC (Australia) provide opportunities to practice medicine abroad without needing FMGE qualification. If you're looking for a faster route, consider PLAB/UKMLA; for higher earning potential, USMLE is a strong choice; and for long-term migration and settlement, AMC can be an excellent option. Explore your global medical career opportunities today.

A federal court ruled that the $100,000 H-1B fee was an unauthorized tax, providing relief to Indian medical graduates, who receive nearly 70% of H-1B approvals. Hospitals can once again sponsor residents without the added financial burden, supporting IMG-friendly residency opportunities. However, the legal battle continues, with an appeal underway and conflicting court decisions that could ultimately be reviewed by the Supreme Court. If you're pursuing USMLE or residency training, stay focused and continue moving forward with your plans.

Starting June 2026, all USMLE accommodation requests must be submitted through the NBME MyUSMLE Portal. This requirement applies to Step 1, Step 2 CK, and Step 3 candidates, including International Medical Graduates (IMGs). The documentation requirements and 60-day review process remain the same. Any pending accommodation requests have been automatically transferred to the new system. Applicants are encouraged to submit requests as early as possible and not wait for exam scheduling approval. Be sure to plan ahead and account for your eligibility period.

Indian IMGs face several major USMLE Step 2 CK challenges, including achieving competitive scores, adapting to clinical reasoning, managing high costs, understanding the MyIntealth process and seven-year rule, gaining USCE, building research profiles, and handling ERAS with time zone differences. These challenges can be managed through strong NBME preparation, alumni networking, PubMed-indexed research, and early planning for a successful residency match.

Indian medical graduates are increasingly opting for the AMC Australia pathway instead of NEET PG because of the intense competition in India, with nearly 1.7 lakh candidates competing for just 74,000 seats and admissions sometimes happening even with negative scores. The AMC route provides salaried hospital positions with annual earnings of around AUD 75,000–95,000, removes the uncertainty of counselling-based seat allocation, and offers a clearer pathway to permanent residency along with a healthier work-life balance. The overall AMC exam process costs approximately INR 5-7 lakh, which is still more affordable than pursuing a private MD in India. The certainty and structured career pathway are major reasons behind this growing trend.

In 2026, many NHS doctors are choosing Australia because of a 26% drop in real-term pay, heavy patient workloads, and limited training opportunities. Australia provides salaries that are 2-3 times higher, fewer weekly patients (114 compared to 205), and a straightforward pathway to permanent residency. Indian MBBS graduates can also move through the AMC or PLAB routes. The total migration cost is around ₹3.5-10 lakhs, which can often be recovered within a few months of working. Applying before the age of 33 gives the best chance to secure maximum PR points.

Indian MBBS graduates can appear for the AMC exam after completing EPIC verification, graduating from a WDOMS-listed medical college, and finishing internship. The Standard Pathway includes AMC Part 1 MCQ (computer-based test, passing score 250/500) followed by AMC Part 2 clinical exam in Melbourne or Workplace-Based Assessment (WBA) in Australia. The full process usually takes around 2.5 to 3.5 years. Begin with EPIC verification before starting question bank preparation.
